instructions.cross_packet_rule: Use cross_packet_terms for likely synonyms, owners, consumers, and seams outside this packet.
instructions.family_key_rule: Every assigned raw family key must have exactly one family_key_assignments row and at least one mapped feature.
instructions.objective: Normalize every assigned validated audit atom into an exhaustive local inventory of distinct Puppet Master features, systems, tools, workflows, GUI surfaces, integrations, data models, governance controls, or cross-cutting concerns. Preserve under-specification, contradictions, unknowns, and explicit non-gaps.
instructions.output_rule: Write exactly one strict-schema JSON payload in the assigned output directory and then return PMR1.
instructions.partition_rule: Every atom_id must appear in exactly one feature.atom_ids array; no omission or duplication.
instructions.research_rule: Do not browse in this phase. Give every normalized feature at least one concrete external-research question for the mandatory next phase; do not treat absence of seed queries as permission to omit research.
instructions.scenario_rule: Give every feature at least one falsifiable scenario requirement for later certification.
instructions.split_merge_rule: Split concepts with distinct lifecycle, authority, consumers, or failure semantics. Merge only true synonyms describing the same product concept; record aliases and relationships instead of collapsing uncertainty.

atoms.statement: PLS-010 enumerates concrete validator failures and requires exact diagnostic reporting through dedicated validation surfaces.
atoms.title: Ledger validation is explicitly falsifiable

atoms.statement: Compile-queue fidelity, pending-seal state, and forbidden downstream artifacts are sharply separated.
atoms.title: Ordinary compile has an explicit terminal boundary

atoms.statement: The closure workflow is semantically exhaustive but does not define append/update atomicity, revision checks, lock ownership, duplicate-writer handling, or crash recovery for the global registry.
atoms.title: Semantic closure registry lacks concurrency control

atoms.statement: The matrices carry strong coverage requirements, but the only matrix-specific validation surface is future work, leaving no current executable completeness oracle in this PlanUnit.
atoms.title: Compile-input matrices are required but not currently enforceable

atoms.statement: PLS-014 is gui_related and defines ledger_sync_blocked behavior, but it does not specify the visible status, disabled-control semantics, accessible announcement, localization, offline distinction, or recovery affordance.
atoms.title: Ledger synchronization failure has no complete GUI truth contract

atoms.statement: The native runtime contract explicitly addresses atomicity, concurrent revision control, idempotency, partial-write blocking, referential integrity, and recovery clearance.
atoms.title: Native ledger durability and recovery are strongly specified

atoms.statement: PLS-016 defines useful fields but not the authoritative storage owner, repository-scoped key identity, or merge/reuse relationship with the existing semantic closure registry and the later PLS-017/PLS-018 concepts.
atoms.title: External finding closure has an unresolved registry seam

atoms.statement: The in-process service boundary and import-package threat checks are explicit, including collision policy requirements.
atoms.title: Native import security is concretely bounded

atoms.statement: User visibility is required, but the displayed closure contract has no required fields, accessible announcement behavior, localization handling, or recovery/reopen affordance.
atoms.title: Bot closure visibility is not a usable GUI contract

atoms.statement: PLS-018 names an ExternalIssueClosureRegistry and two fragments of acceptance behavior but provides no record schema, state machine, authority model, persistence owner, evidence-quality rule, or executable validator.
atoms.title: P1 external issue closure is not implementation-ready

secure exact-source archival redaction retention tombstones audit lineage
accessible localized offline synchronization blocked UI recovery patterns

atoms.statement: Planning Wizard has exactly three structured, provenance-preserving seed families, while Chain Wizard and Plan Wizard remain retired compatibility lineage and the handoff cannot be an unbounded raw transcript.
atoms.title: Canonical planning intake and naming boundary

atoms.statement: One PlanningRun groups bounded topic, integration, and audit threads while owning the durable aggregate and representing project context independently from compatible work intents.
atoms.title: PlanningRun aggregate and bounded thread topology

atoms.statement: The evidence-driven topic graph is mutable through explicit controller operations that preserve reasons, dependencies, origins, and downstream invalidations while the GUI may suggest an order without overriding the graph.
atoms.title: Dynamic topic graph operations

atoms.statement: Fresh topic agents receive bounded capsules and must durably synchronize substantive turns; safe defaults and evidence resolve ordinary gaps, while destructive, credential, legal, risk, and irreconcilable-policy choices remain HITL authority boundaries.
atoms.title: Bounded topic-agent autonomy and HITL boundary

atoms.statement: Topic and global records share one Planning Run ledger; material later decisions invalidate dependent drafts, and changed approved intent is represented by clarification, immutable amendment, scope disposition, or successor-PRD request rather than in-place mutation.
atoms.title: Typed invalidation and immutable PRD amendments

atoms.statement: Topic closure requires versioned conversion with lineage followed by an independent audit-repair-reaudit loop; only a pass or typed blocker closes the loop, while high-risk decisions may invoke policy-scoped HITL.
atoms.title: Topic conversion and independent audit loop

atoms.statement: Final integration reconciles all Ready topic drafts, and visual references remain supporting evidence whose material implications must be duplicated into canonical textual requirements and ledger records.
atoms.title: Final integration and text-canonical visual evidence

atoms.statement: Read-only project discovery is automatic, but repository mutations require policy and receipts; remote projects stay remote without local fallback, and implementation worktree preparation remains Executor-owned after Plan Compile.
atoms.title: Project discovery and mutation authority boundary

atoms.statement: PWIZ-009 enumerates testing-intake content and names the downstream automated testing system, but it does not define the payload identity/version, required versus optional fields, delivery acknowledgement, idempotency, partial-failure handling, or a falsifiable end-to-end handoff oracle.
atoms.title: Testing-topic handoff is not mechanically specified

atoms.statement: Approve And Build creates the immutable ApprovedPlanPack authority, immediately creates or resumes exactly one PlanCompileRun in product runtime, preserves Executor-owned execution context, and navigates to Orchestrator Plan Compile without a second ordinary Start Build step.
atoms.title: ApprovedPlanPack and Approve And Build authority

atoms.statement: Approve And Build is a fail-closed CAS over every displayed currentness input; success atomically records approval and binds one synchronous PlanCompileRun identity, while duplicate delivery is idempotent and stale input returns to bounded revalidation or review refresh.
atoms.title: Approval CAS and idempotent PlanCompileRun binding

atoms.statement: Topic and final-pack audits use stable, hash-bound findings and bounded repair/re-audit loops; specialists remain read-only and parallel, while the controller or canonical owner serializes writes and certification.
atoms.title: Product-native specialist audit and sole-writer repair

atoms.statement: Compile readiness requires synchronized, audited, current, traceable inputs and a zero-incomplete gate; any exception must identify the exact span, risk, approver, disposition, and reopen condition, and unsupported invented claims are defects.
atoms.title: Zero-incomplete compile-readiness oracle

atoms.statement: PWIZ-013 specifies a twelve-state operational GUI vocabulary, but the later repair addendum declares a different eleven-state vocabulary and five commands; neither text reconciles the vocabularies or provides a transition table, leaving the canonical state machine internally contradictory.
atoms.title: Planning topic state vocabularies conflict

atoms.statement: Planning Wizard source pickers consume DiscoveryService with project/host and policy context, expose stale and failure states without leaking hidden candidates, and treat selections only as planning evidence pending exact implementation-time verification.
atoms.title: Policy-aware planning source picker

atoms.statement: PWIZ-016 defines immutable project-scoped history, compare/export/reopen/send-forward behavior, and forever-by-default retention for final outputs, but it does not specify deletion or erasure authority, legal-hold precedence, quota and storage-pressure behavior, corruption recovery, export failure handling, or lifecycle oracles for retained drafts versus immutable packs.
atoms.title: Historical plan-pack retention lacks a complete lifecycle

atoms.statement: Completed or skipped first-run setup lands on Planning Wizard; skipped or unhealthy provider state remains a nonblocking limited mode with exact warning copy and a Set up provider CTA, while structured onboarding state and warnings are preserved.
atoms.title: First-run limited-provider landing state

atoms.statement: Final review must distinguish Captured, Plan-complete, and Buildable; Approve And Build remains disabled while the buildability report fails, shows all open blocker families and owner docs, and treats PNC-019 as a hard reason only while its live projection is hard-disabled.
atoms.title: Fail-closed implementation buildability gate
